entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Accordingly claimed that the claimant is entitled for interest as contemplated under law.
In view of these facts, it is just and necessary to note the relevant provisions regarding rate of interest as well as depositing of the award amount to the Court.
Admittedly, the claimant/respondent No.2 filed writ petitions to award compensation as per New Act, that has been allowed.
Further, the land acquisition proceedings also subsequent to the New Act.
As such, certainly New Act is applicable to the facts of this case.

Section 80 of the New Act speaks about the payment of interest, which reads as under:
"80.
Payment
of interest

: When the amount of such compensation is not paid or deposited on or before taking possession of the land, the Collector shall pay the amount awarded with interest thereon at the rate of nine per cent.
per annum from the time of so L.A.C. No. 104/2022 C/w L.A.C. No. 106/2022 taking possession until it shall have been so paid or deposited

:
Provided that if such compensation or any part thereof is not paid or deposited within a period of one year from the date on which possession is taken, interest at the rate of fifteen per cent. per annum shall be payable from the date or expiry of the said period of one year on the amount of compensation or part thereof which has not been paid or deposited before the date of such expiry."
In the case on hand, admittedly, the General Award passed on 11.09.2018 and Final Notification has been issued on 22.08.2018.

It is undisputed fact that once the Final Notification has been issued regarding acquisition of property, then it has to be accepted that the beneficiary has taken possession of the property unless and until the petitioner/beneficiary make out specific case that they have not taken possession of the property as on the date of Final Notification or possession of the property has been continued with the owner of the L.A.C. No. 104/2022 C/w L.A.C. No.
106/2022 property.

In the case on hand, the claimant/respondent No.2 has not claimed the specific date in which date he has lost possession and even the beneficiary or petitioner has not made out any case to show when actually taken over possession.
Admittedly, the award has been passed on 11.09.2018.

Hence, in the case on hand, it can be safely inferred that possession of the property has been taken by the beneficiary or petitioner as on 11.09.018 i.e., from the date of passing of award.
.12.
